items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: I was 22 when I played with Billie.

ctx.x: When we read in your bios that you performed early on with Billie Holiday and John Coltrane and Cecil Taylor, I think it’s hard for us to go back to that time and imagine what were those musicians, what was their reputation at the time. Were your knees shaking because, oh I’m playing with John Coltrane?

Not so much John because at that point John was one of the respected tenor players of the day, not the icon that he later became. I certainly liked his playing in some ways I want to say that I liked his earlier playing better than some of his later music for a number of reasons that I have explored a lot in the book that I’m writing, how the music changed and what different things influenced it. Billie Holiday I certainly knew how revered she was and that was — was that a year earlier? I can’t remember if that…

I related to that immediately because I was lucky enough to play behind Aretha Franklin once in the saxophone section, and I found that within the first five minutes that I had to stop paying attention to her because I wasn’t covering my part.
